text: Now the two hypotheses, and keep them as two separate drawings. The first and older one is the lock-and-key hypothesis. The active site has a fixed shape that is complementary to the substrate before the substrate arrives, like a lock cut for one key. The substrate fits, the complex forms, the products leave, and the active site has the same shape throughout. This is not a wrong picture: when June 2024 asked for diagrams of the lock-and-key hypothesis for lysozyme, those diagrams earned the marks. It is the simpler model, and it explains specificity.
